commit_message:
[Codegen][SPIRV] Add Initial Conv2d Tiling for VideocoreVII

Follow-up on the previous PR.

The Broadcom VideoCore VII (RPi5 GPU) has 32 threads per workgroup
and 16 KiB of workgroup memory. Memory could not be derived explicitly
but was assumed from previous generations. Both characteristics are
an order of magnitude smaller than the GPU default the SPIRV conv
config defines. So its workgroup tile and pipeline choices overflow
the device.

This PR therefore introduces a variant of the conv2d tiling configuration
chosen around a power-of-two divisor at each level that attempts to keep
loads coalesced within the VideoCore's budget. We restrict the support for
this config to NCHW f32 conv and depthwise for now. NHWC and non-f32 are
intentionally rejected so the default path stays for those cases.
name: setup / setup

[Codegen][SPIRV] Add Initial Conv2d Tiling for VideocoreVII

Follow-up on the previous PR.

The Broadcom VideoCore VII (RPi5 GPU) has 32 threads per workgroup
and 16 KiB of workgroup memory. Memory could not be derived explicitly
but was assumed from previous generations. Both characteristics are
an order of magnitude smaller than the GPU default the SPIRV conv
config defines. So its workgroup tile and pipeline choices overflow
the device.

This PR therefore introduces a variant of the conv2d tiling configuration
chosen around a power-of-two divisor at each level that attempts to keep
loads coalesced within the VideoCore's budget. We restrict the support for
this config to NCHW f32 conv and depthwise for now. NHWC and non-f32 are
intentionally rejected so the default path stays for those cases.
name: runtime :: ubuntu-24.04

commit_message:
[Codegen][SPIRV] Add Initial Conv2d Tiling for VideocoreVII

Follow-up on the previous PR.

The Broadcom VideoCore VII (RPi5 GPU) has 32 threads per workgroup
and 16 KiB of workgroup memory. Memory could not be derived explicitly
but was assumed from previous generations. Both characteristics are
an order of magnitude smaller than the GPU default the SPIRV conv
config defines. So its workgroup tile and pipeline choices overflow
the device.

This PR therefore introduces a variant of the conv2d tiling configuration
chosen around a power-of-two divisor at each level that attempts to keep
loads coalesced within the VideoCore's budget. We restrict the support for
this config to NCHW f32 conv and depthwise for now. NHWC and non-f32 are
intentionally rejected so the default path stays for those cases.
name: Test ONNX

commit_message:
[Runtime] Guard against NULL frontier_tracker in standalone HIP/CUDA devices (#24474)

`iree_hal_hip_device_advance_frontier` (and its CUDA counterpart) is
called on every `queue_execute`, including plain buffer transfers. For
standalone devices, not assigned to a device group via
`iree_hal_device_assign_topology_info`, `frontier_tracker` is `NULL,
causing a crash during invocation of
`iree_hal_hip_device_advance_frontier`.

This commit adds a NULL early-return guard.

Signed-off-by: Abhishek Varma <abhvarma@amd.com>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[HAL] Implement functions to normalize buffer references and buffer bindings to subspan buffers (#24472)

Buffer references and bindings can point to subspans of buffers. HAL
drivers need to handle this case and access the actual memory allocation
in the underlying allocated buffer. This can be handled by normalizing
buffer references and buffer bindings before processing those.
Normalization means to replace the reference to (a part of) a subspan
buffer with a reference to the corresponding part of the underlying
allocated buffer in the buffer reference or buffer binding.

This change provides functions that perform those normalizations as
helpers/infrastructure for HAL drivers.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

drivers need to handle this case and access the actual memory allocation
in the underlying allocated buffer. This can be handled by normalizing
buffer references and buffer bindings before processing those.

buffer with a reference to the corresponding part of the underlying
allocated buffer in the buffer reference or buffer binding.

Buffer references and bindings can point to subspans of buffers. HAL
drivers need to handle this case and access the actual memory allocation
in the underlying allocated buffer. This can be handled by normalizing
buffer references and buffer bindings before processing those.
Normalization means to replace the reference to (a part of) a subspan
buffer with a reference to the corresponding part of the underlying
allocated buffer in the buffer reference or buffer binding.

This change provides functions that perform those normalizations as
helpers/infrastructure for HAL drivers.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>
name: Test ONNX / test_onnx_ops :: cpu_llvm_sync_O2

commit_message:
Add chipDetails for RDNA3 (#24419)

Add `perfTflops` and `memoryBandwidthTbps` to get precise
`computeMemoryCutoff ` value for each RDNA3 SKU.

The new GEMM size cutoff value on W7900 brings more improvements than
regressions across a sample set of GEMM shapes, with an avg improvement
of **~10%**. See data
[here](https://gist.github.com/RattataKing/fddaf22bf0807fae0961240bc9847d78).

---------

Signed-off-by: Amily Wu <amilywu2@amd.com>
name: linux_x64_gcc

commit_message:
[Codegen][SPIRV] Add Initial Conv2d Tiling for VideocoreVII

Follow-up on the previous PR.

The Broadcom VideoCore VII (RPi5 GPU) has 32 threads per workgroup
and 16 KiB of workgroup memory. Memory could not be derived explicitly
but was assumed from previous generations. Both characteristics are
an order of magnitude smaller than the GPU default the SPIRV conv
config defines. So its workgroup tile and pipeline choices overflow
the device.

This PR therefore introduces a variant of the conv2d tiling configuration
chosen around a power-of-two divisor at each level that attempts to keep
loads coalesced within the VideoCore's budget. We restrict the support for
this config to NCHW f32 conv and depthwise for now. NHWC and non-f32 are
intentionally rejected so the default path stays for those cases.
name: setup / setup

The Broadcom VideoCore VII (RPi5 GPU) has 32 threads per workgroup
and 16 KiB of workgroup memory. Memory could not be derived explicitly
but was assumed from previous generations. Both characteristics are
an order of magnitude smaller than the GPU default the SPIRV conv
config defines. So its workgroup tile and pipeline choices overflow
the device.

This PR therefore introduces a variant of the conv2d tiling configuration
chosen around a power-of-two divisor at each level that attempts to keep
loads coalesced within the VideoCore's budget. We restrict the support for
this config to NCHW f32 conv and depthwise for now. NHWC and non-f32 are
intentionally rejected so the default path stays for those cases.
name: Test ONNX / test_onnx_ops :: amdgpu_vulkan_rdna3_O0

commit_message:
[Codegen][SPIRV] Add Initial Conv2d Tiling for VideocoreVII

Follow-up on the previous PR.

The Broadcom VideoCore VII (RPi5 GPU) has 32 threads per workgroup
and 16 KiB of workgroup memory. Memory could not be derived explicitly
but was assumed from previous generations. Both characteristics are
an order of magnitude smaller than the GPU default the SPIRV conv
config defines. So its workgroup tile and pipeline choices overflow
the device.

This PR therefore introduces a variant of the conv2d tiling configuration
chosen around a power-of-two divisor at each level that attempts to keep
loads coalesced within the VideoCore's budget. We restrict the support for
this config to NCHW f32 conv and depthwise for now. NHWC and non-f32 are
intentionally rejected so the default path stays for those cases.
name: linux_x64_gcc

commit_message:
Add chipDetails for RDNA3 (#24419)

Add `perfTflops` and `memoryBandwidthTbps` to get precise
`computeMemoryCutoff ` value for each RDNA3 SKU.

The new GEMM size cutoff value on W7900 brings more improvements than
regressions across a sample set of GEMM shapes, with an avg improvement
of **~10%**. See data
[here](https://gist.github.com/RattataKing/fddaf22bf0807fae0961240bc9847d78).

commit_message:
[Codegen] Split StableHLO/JAX select-style argmax reductions (#24445)

Problem:
StableHLO/JAX lowers argmax for lm_head vocab reductions as a pair of
selects with explicit NaN handling and lower-index tie breaking. The
existing split-reduction matcher only recognized the canonical
maximumf/cmpf/select form, so large vocab reductions stayed as one wide
reduction.

Fix:
Teach the argmax matcher to distinguish canonical and StableHLO/JAX
select-style argmax reductions, and preserve the corresponding combiner
when splitting. Keep the select-style matcher strict by requiring the
`gt || isnan` value condition, the `eq && lower_index` tie condition,
and the expected value/index select operands.

Example:
A Qwen `lm_head` argmax over vocab size 248320 can now split into a
two-stage reduction over 1940x128 tiles while preserving NaN and
lower-index tie semantics. Negative tests ensure similar-looking select
reductions with different NaN/tie/index semantics do not split.

---------

Signed-off-by: Yuwei Sun <yuweis2@illinois.edu>
Signed-off-by: Hao Ren <rhao8608@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Hao Ren <rhao8608@gmail.com>

commit_message:
[Codegen] Split StableHLO/JAX select-style argmax reductions (#24445)

Problem:
StableHLO/JAX lowers argmax for lm_head vocab reductions as a pair of
selects with explicit NaN handling and lower-index tie breaking. The
existing split-reduction matcher only recognized the canonical
maximumf/cmpf/select form, so large vocab reductions stayed as one wide
reduction.

Fix:
Teach the argmax matcher to distinguish canonical and StableHLO/JAX
select-style argmax reductions, and preserve the corresponding combiner
when splitting. Keep the select-style matcher strict by requiring the
`gt || isnan` value condition, the `eq && lower_index` tie condition,
and the expected value/index select operands.

Example:
A Qwen `lm_head` argmax over vocab size 248320 can now split into a
two-stage reduction over 1940x128 tiles while preserving NaN and
lower-index tie semantics. Negative tests ensure similar-looking select
reductions with different NaN/tie/index semantics do not split.

commit_message:
[Codegen][SPIRV] Add Initial Conv2d Tiling for VideocoreVII (#24548)

Follow-up on the previous PR.

The Broadcom VideoCore VII (RPi5 GPU) has 32 threads per workgroup and
16 KiB of workgroup memory. Memory could not be derived explicitly from
vulkaninfo but was assumed from previous generations. Both
characteristics are an order of magnitude smaller than the GPU default
the SPIRV conv config defines. So its workgroup tile and pipeline
choices overflow the device.

This PR therefore introduces a variant of the conv2d tiling
configuration chosen around a power-of-two divisor at each level that
attempts to keep loads coalesced within the VideoCore's budget. We
restrict the support for this config to NCHW f32 conv and depthwise for
now. NHWC and non-f32 are intentionally rejected so the default path
stays for those cases.

---------

Co-authored-by: Artem Gindinson <gindinson@roofline.ai>

[Codegen][SPIRV] Add Initial Conv2d Tiling for VideocoreVII (#24548)

Follow-up on the previous PR.

The Broadcom VideoCore VII (RPi5 GPU) has 32 threads per workgroup and
16 KiB of workgroup memory. Memory could not be derived explicitly from
vulkaninfo but was assumed from previous generations. Both
characteristics are an order of magnitude smaller than the GPU default
the SPIRV conv config defines. So its workgroup tile and pipeline
choices overflow the device.

This PR therefore introduces a variant of the conv2d tiling
configuration chosen around a power-of-two divisor at each level that
attempts to keep loads coalesced within the VideoCore's budget. We
restrict the support for this config to NCHW f32 conv and depthwise for
now. NHWC and non-f32 are intentionally rejected so the default path
stays for those cases.

---------

commit_message:
[Codegen][SPIRV] Add Initial Conv2d Tiling for VideocoreVII (#24548)

Follow-up on the previous PR.

The Broadcom VideoCore VII (RPi5 GPU) has 32 threads per workgroup and
16 KiB of workgroup memory. Memory could not be derived explicitly from
vulkaninfo but was assumed from previous generations. Both
characteristics are an order of magnitude smaller than the GPU default
the SPIRV conv config defines. So its workgroup tile and pipeline
choices overflow the device.

This PR therefore introduces a variant of the conv2d tiling
configuration chosen around a power-of-two divisor at each level that
attempts to keep loads coalesced within the VideoCore's budget. We
restrict the support for this config to NCHW f32 conv and depthwise for
now. NHWC and non-f32 are intentionally rejected so the default path
stays for those cases.

commit_message:
Add chipDetails for RDNA3 (#24419)

Add `perfTflops` and `memoryBandwidthTbps` to get precise
`computeMemoryCutoff ` value for each RDNA3 SKU.

The new GEMM size cutoff value on W7900 brings more improvements than
regressions across a sample set of GEMM shapes, with an avg improvement
of **~10%**. See data
[here](https://gist.github.com/RattataKing/fddaf22bf0807fae0961240bc9847d78).

---------

Signed-off-by: Amily Wu <amilywu2@amd.com>
name: macos_x64_clang
